title: Research
lead: My work asks how geometric constraints, such as bounded curvature or a minimum thickness, shape the topology and the optimal configurations of curves, ribbons and disk systems.

themes.title: Variational rigidity and contact strata
body: A unified variational method for disk diagrams, finite packing problems and perimeter minimisation under geometric constraints. Configurations are stratified by their *contact graphs* (which disks touch), and the admissible deformations at each stratum are governed by the active contacts.
First- and second-order variational analysis on these strata gives a systematic way to decide when a configuration is rigid, when it can flex, and when it is minimal.

themes.title: Critical ribbon loops and Gordian unknots
body: Ribbons of fixed width and curvature bound can be topologically trivial and still be geometrically locked. The *Gordian unknot conjecture* asserts that such geometrically distinct unknots exist, and that they cannot be untied through constrained deformations.
The same ideas extend to links, where one studies *Gordian unlinks* and the geometric constraints that obstruct link isotopy.

themes.title: Bounded curvature paths
body: A bounded curvature path is a $C^1$ and piecewise $C^2$ path in a manifold $M$ joining two elements of the tangent bundle $TM$, with curvature bounded by a positive constant. In 1961 Lester Dubins raised the question of the homotopy classes of such paths in the plane; my doctoral dissertation closes the programme he proposed.

Let $\Gamma(n)$ be the space of bounded curvature paths with fixed endpoints in $T\mathbb{R}^2$ and winding number $n$. Four *proximity conditions* on the endpoints give qualitative insight into the topology of $\Gamma(n)$, for instance the number of homotopy classes it contains.

The shortest elements of $\Gamma(n)$ are classified for every $n$ and every pair of endpoints, recovering the CSC and CCC characterisation of Dubins (1957). A continuity argument ensures the curvature bound is never violated during a deformation, which yields the classification of homotopy classes, including classes made exclusively of embedded paths.

themes.title: Polytopes and dynamics
body: Joint work on compression maps between polytopes, and on topological dynamics over finite directed graphs.
